legend: Given a sequence of integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ0%% and a prime number x%%ZSMJ1%%.

We have a function which takes length%%ZSMJ2%% as a parameter and return the maximum possible value of  (a_i\times a_{i+1}\times \cdots \times a_{i+length-1})\pmod x%%ZSMJ3%% , where 1 \le i \le (n-length+1) %%ZSMJ4%%.
Your task is to find the smallest length for which this function return maximum possible value.
input: The first line contains a single integer t (1 \le t \le 10^5)%%ZSMJ14%% — the number of test cases in the input. Then t%%ZSMJ15%% test cases follow.

Each query contains two lines. The first line contains two integer n (1 \le n \le 10^5)%%ZSMJ16%%: the number of integers in the sequence and x (2 \le x \le 97)%%ZSMJ17%%, and the second line contains n%%ZSMJ18%% integers a_1, \ldots ,a_n (1\le a_i  \lt  x)%%ZSMJ19%%.
It is guaranteed that the total sum of n%%ZSMJ20%% is at most 10^5%%ZSMJ21%% and x%%ZSMJ22%% be a prime number.
output: Print t%%ZSMJ23%% answers to the test cases. Each answer must be consisting of two integers — the maximum possible value of function and the smallest length for which function return maximum possible value.
note: In the first query — Explained in Problem Statement. For length = 1%%ZSMJ24%% and 3%%ZSMJ25%%, Function return maximum value i.e 4%%ZSMJ26%%. We have to return the minimum length i.e 1%%ZSMJ27%%.
